chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu'l-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Rahim ibn Ali ibn Sa'id al-Jabali narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Nasr al-Khazzaz narrated to us. He said: Amr ibn Talha narrated to us from Asbat ibn Nasr, from Simak ibn Harb, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.
He said: I came to Abdullah ibn Abbas and said to him: O cousin of the Messenger of Allah! I have come to ask you about Ali ibn Abi Talib and the people's differing regarding him.

So Ibn Abbas said: O Ibn Jubayr! You have come to ask me about the best of God's creation in the community after Muhammad, the Prophet of God. You have come to ask me about a man who had three thousand virtues in a single night — and that is the Night of al-Qurba.

O Ibn Jubayr! You have come to ask me about the deputy of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and his minister, and his vicegerent, and the master of his Pond, his Banner, and his intercession.

By Him in whose hand is the soul of Ibn Abbas! If the oceans of the world were ink, and its trees were pens, and its people were scribes, and they wrote the virtues and excellences of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) from the day God — Mighty and Majestic — created the world until He brings it to an end, they would not reach even a tenth of what God — Blessed and Exalted — has granted him.

key_terms.لَيْلَة الْقُرْبَة: The Night of Nearness/Proximity — a specific night on which, according to this tradition, three thousand angels came to Ali, each greeting him with a new salutation (virtue)
key_terms.مَنْقَبَة: A virtue, merit, or excellence; plural manaqib — the technical term for literature extolling the virtues of Ali and the Imams
key_terms.مِعْشَار: A tenth (literally one-tenth); used here hyperbolically to indicate that even the smallest fraction of Ali's virtues could not be recorded
key_terms.وَصِيّ: Deputy/legatee — designates the person the Prophet appointed as his executor and successor; a key term in Shia theology

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn Abbas say about the virtues of Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: This hadith records a famous declaration by Ibn Abbas, the Prophet's cousin and greatest Companion-exegete, in response to Sa'id ibn Jubayr's question about Ali ibn Abi Talib. Ibn Abbas extols Ali as the best of creation after the Prophet, describes the Night of al-Qurba when Ali received three thousand virtues, and names him the Prophet's deputy, minister, vicegerent, and the master of his Pond, Banner, and intercession. The closing hyperbolic oath — that even if all the world's oceans were ink and all its trees were pens, scribes could not enumerate a tenth of Ali's God-given merits — mirrors Quranic language (Q 18:109, 31:27) and conveys the limitlessness of Imam Ali's station.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Muhammad b. Musa (ra) narrated to us. He said: Abu’l `Abbas Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr b. `Abdullah b. Habib narrated to us. He said: `Abd al-Rahman b. `Ali b. Sa`id al-Jabali narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Nasr al-Khazzaz narrated to us. He said: `Amr b. Talha narrated to us from Asbat b. Nasr from Simak b. Harb from Sa`id b. Jubayr.
He said: I met `Abdullah b. `Abbas and said to him: O cousin of the Messenger of Allah! I have come to you to ask you about `Ali b. Abi Talib and the people’s differing over him.

So, Ibn `Abbas said: O Ibn Jubayr! You have come to me to ask me about the best of the creation in the Nation after Muhammad the prophet of Allah. You have come to me to ask me about a man who received three thousand virtues in one night, and that is the Night of al-Qurba (when three thousand angels greeted `Ali).
O Ibn Jubayr! You have come to me to ask me about the deputy of the Messenger of Allah (s) and his vizier, his vicegerent (khalifa), and the master of his Pond, his Banner, and his intercession.

By Him in whose hand is the soul of Ibn `Abbas! Had the oceans of this world been ink, and had its trees been pens, and had its people been scribes, and they wrote the qualities and virtues of `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) from the day Allah created this world until the day He ends it, they would not be able to exhaust all of what Allah has given him.
